action.description: No implementation action at the root; this node records the initial analysis and branches into mutually exclusive first-kernel ownership plans.
action.rationale: Root is a dummy decision point required by the world model.
action.title: Analysis root

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX 5090 Mobile has ample FP32/FP16 throughput, 82 SMs, 32-wide waves, 64 MB L2, but HLSL cs_6_8 path limits groupshared memory to 32 KiB per threadgroup.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The workload is small fixed-window dense linear algebra plus softmax; hardware fit is good, but HLSL tensor-core access is uncertain and scalar code may dominate.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Incorrect use of groupshared or excessive scalar reductions could underuse the GPU despite high theoretical throughput.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input and output alone are about 118 MB each, while all model weights are tiny and should remain resident in L2; avoiding global intermediates is the largest bandwidth win.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Repeated state reads per token/window can create heavy L2 traffic if weights are not staged or reused effectively.

register_pressure.notes: Full fusion is plausible because C=32 and N=16 are fixed, but q/k/v, softmax rows, MLP accumulators, and layernorm temporaries can quickly exceed comfortable per-thread registers.
register_pressure.risk: A naive all-in-register mapping may reduce occupancy or spill, especially when fc1/fc2 accumulators are kept for many channels.

nodes.notes: Evidence now includes a passed fused HLSL implementation at 5.992704 ms vs 10.5455 ms reference, 1.76x speedup. The root family choice space remains useful: ownership granularity is the dominant architectural branch, while lower-level tactics should be chained below the successful single-window family.

action.description: Implement a full fused shader where one threadgroup owns one 4x4 window and computes LN1, QKV, attention, projection, residual, LN2, MLP, and final write without global intermediates. Use registers for owner-local reductions/accumulators and a compact q/k/v groupshared exchange only where cross-token attention needs it.
action.rationale: This directly exploits the fixed small window and channel dimensions, eliminates all intermediate global round-trips, and keeps the ownership model simple enough for a first correct high-performance kernel.
action.title: Single-window full-block ownership

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: 57600 windows provide enough groups for 82 SMs; C=32 and N=16 align naturally with 32-lane waves and small reductions.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Wave-size reductions align well with C=32, enabling one lane per channel and efficient WaveActiveSum patterns. It still uses scalar FP32/FP16 conversions rather than tensor cores, but the small dimensions favor wave-level scalar execution.

memory_bandwidth.notes: One group per window reloads small weights for each window, but it writes only final output and keeps most per-window intermediates on-chip. The measured 1.76x speedup shows traffic is acceptable for the fixed C=32,H=128 shape.

register_pressure.notes: The full fused schedule has nontrivial live ranges and shared exchange buffers, but limiting ownership to one 4x4 window keeps pressure manageable compared with attempted batching.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: The passed single-window family assigns one threadgroup to one 4x4 window and fuses the entire transformer-like block, using wave reductions for 32-channel dot products and writing only final output. This matches the compact-window shape and avoids staging global intermediate tensors.
- bottleneck: remaining cost is mostly sync and scalar transcendental/MLP compute, with some repeated tiny-weight bandwidth.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes.
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- The sibling window-batch attempt was much slower, which increases confidence that the smaller ownership granularity is the safer end-to-end mapping for this HLSL/DXIL runner. The prior 1.76x speedup is now the best evidence-backed path.
- next bet: Apply a lifetime refinement under this node: reuse one compact groupshared weight/input tile per phase and keep owner-local values in registers to reduce simultaneous shared residency and barriers without changing ownership.
SELF_CHECK: This root child is mutually exclusive with window_batch_full_block_owner and output_token_block_owner because the full block for exactly one 4x4 window is owned by one threadgroup.

action.description: Implement a fused shader where one threadgroup owns a small batch of adjacent 4x4 windows and runs the complete block for all of them, using the repeated model state across those windows to reduce per-window state traffic while still writing only final outputs.
action.rationale: Model weights are tiny but reused for every window; batching windows inside a group can amortize cooperative state movement and improve arithmetic per synchronization if register/shared-memory pressure remains controlled.
action.title: Window-batch full-block ownership

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: The 32 KiB HLSL groupshared limit constrains simultaneous state tiles plus per-window q/k/v exchange buffers; larger groups may reduce occupancy on 82 SMs.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The shader uses wave reductions over C=32 and scalar FP32 math/exp/tanh rather than tensor cores. Larger window batches increase scalar work and barriers without improving hardware fit.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The intended batching should amortize tiny state tensors, but measured latency indicates weight/state reuse was not enough to offset extra per-group work, occupancy loss, and synchronization. Input/output traffic is small relative to redundant arithmetic and intermediate movement.

register_pressure.notes: Batching adjacent windows increases live values and intermediate arrays; even with groupshared staging, the full fused block stresses registers and occupancy. This likely reduces active warps and hides memory latency poorly.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: The current solution launches one 256-thread group per 4x4 window despite the node intent of batching multiple adjacent windows; it fuses LN, QKV, attention, projection, second LN, MLP, and final residual for all 16 tokens. It uses gs_tmp/gs_big/gs_attn/gs_res as cross-wave exchange buffers and intermediate storage, with repeated group-wide barriers between phases.
- bottleneck: sync/latency and occupancy/register pressure dominate; bandwidth savings from model-state reuse did not materialize.
- groupshared classification: gs_tmp is an exchange buffer for normalized token vectors and attention outputs, produced by token/wave owners and consumed by projection/MLP waves with one reuse per phase; gs_big is an exchange buffer for QKV and hidden activations, produced by reduction waves and consumed by attention/MLP output waves with limited reuse; gs_attn is an exchange buffer for softmax rows, produced by lane-0 attention row owners and consumed by value accumulation threads; gs_res is an exchange buffer for residual values, produced after attention projection and consumed by LN2/output. Each cross-thread read requires the following GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync, causing phase-by-phase synchronization.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: no.
- if_no: Expected intent was one threadgroup owning a small batch of adjacent windows to amortize repeated model-state movement. The implemented code still maps one group to one window, while adding a heavy full-block fused schedule with many shared-memory exchanges.
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- The evaluation passed numerically but was much slower than reference: 25.129 ms vs 9.154 ms, only 0.364x speedup. This strongly downgrades the window-batch family as currently realized and suggests that full-block ownership with excessive barriers is fragile.
- next bet: Return to the proven single-window full-block owner and refine shared-memory lifetime/weight tiling, because the single-window result already matched the expected latency factor and avoids the failed batching overhead. If this family is revisited, first repair the implementation to actually batch windows and stream a single reusable tile rather than retaining many phase buffers.
PERF_GAP:
- expected: latency factor about 0.48x baseline/reference from batching state reuse.
- observed: latency factor about 2.75x reference, equivalent to 0.364x speedup.
- hypothesized_reason: implementation mismatch plus high synchronization count, extra exchange-buffer traffic, scalar reductions, and lower occupancy overwhelmed any state-reuse benefit.
SELF_CHECK: This root child is mutually exclusive with single_window_full_block_owner and output_token_block_owner because ownership is intended to cover a batch of windows per group, not one window or one output row/token.

action.description: Implement a fused shader where work is owned by output tokens or attention rows rather than whole windows, streaming or recomputing peer token quantities as needed and minimizing groupshared exchange. Preserve single-dispatch final-output-only behavior.
action.rationale: This is a lower-shared-memory fallback that may simplify synchronization and avoid the 32 KiB groupshared constraint, at the cost of redundant QKV/LN and state reads.
action.title: Output-token / attention-row ownership

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Token-level ownership creates far more independent work items but each has small reductions over C=32 and N=16, which may map well to waves but poorly to tensor cores.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Attention rows map naturally to wave reductions, but MLP/projection phases would become fragmented and lose cross-phase fusion. This is less compelling after the single-window full-block evidence.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Per-token or per-attention-row ownership risks rereading weights and token activations many times and may require materializing phase outputs to UAV/SRV because the current runner is single-dispatch without graph staging.

register_pressure.notes: Smaller owner units reduce per-group live state and may improve occupancy, but that benefit is likely offset by more dispatch work units and redundant loads.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: Open alternative would assign ownership to individual output tokens or attention rows rather than completing a full window/block in one group. It has no attached implementation yet.
- bottleneck: expected bandwidth/materialization and redundant state loads are the main risks; latency could also rise from fragmented ownership.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes, still open and not evaluated.
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- The failed heavy window-batch result shows that larger ownership is risky, but it does not prove per-row ownership is better; the proven single-window full-block path remains stronger. This node is kept as an alternative, but downscored because fragmentation may forfeit fusion benefits.
- next bet: Only explore this after exhausting single-window refinements, or if register/sync profiling shows full-block fusion cannot improve further.
SELF_CHECK: This root child is mutually exclusive with the full-block window owners because ownership would be per token/row rather than per complete window or window batch.

action.title: Single reused shared/input tile per phase

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Preserves the good C=32 wave-reduction mapping from the single-window owner while targeting fewer barriers and less shared-memory traffic.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The small state tensors can be streamed or cooperatively staged phase-by-phase, reducing repeated loads without retaining all weights or intermediate tensors in groupshared at once.

register_pressure.notes: Reusing one tile and keeping single-owner intermediates in registers should shorten live ranges and reduce shared allocation pressure versus simultaneous gs buffers.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: Open refinement under the passed single-window owner; replace simultaneous phase buffers/weight residency with a single reused groupshared tile where it has true cross-thread reuse, and otherwise keep values in registers. No attached implementation yet.
- bottleneck: expected bottleneck is sync/shared-memory lifetime, not raw bandwidth.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes, this is a composable child refinement of the best evidence-backed family.
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- The bad window-batch result makes a conservative refinement of the known-good single-window mapping more attractive than changing top-level ownership. Reducing barriers and shared residency should address the current shader's most likely overhead without risking major remapping.
- next bet: Implement this next; classify every groupshared array as either a reusable read-only tile, exchange buffer, or reduction scratch, and remove phase barriers where values are register-owned or wave-local.

action.title: Repair batched-window path with streamed reusable tile

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Does not change the scalar wave-reduction compute pattern; improvement would come from fewer barriers and less shared traffic, not better tensor-core fit.

memory_bandwidth.notes: If actual adjacent-window batching is implemented, a streamed shared tile could amortize small model-state loads across windows. Expected benefit is limited because weights are tiny and likely L2-resident.

register_pressure.notes: Still inherits the larger ownership unit's occupancy risk, but streaming one tile and dropping unnecessary exchange buffers may reduce live state enough to make the family testable.

kernel_summary: This is a fixed-shape, dense, windowed Swin block inference kernel: 57600 independent 4x4 windows over NHWC fp16 input with C=32, single-head N=16 attention, two fp32-accumulating LayerNorm reductions, several tiny dense linear layers, softmax, GELU, and residuals. The best hypothesis is a maximally fused single-dispatch shader that writes only the final tensor, because temporary buffers and multi-dispatch are unavailable and global intermediate traffic would dominate. Model state is only about 25 KiB and highly reused, while q/k/v per window is about 3 KiB; groupshared should be used selectively as a q/k/v exchange buffer and possibly as a compact read-only state tile, not as a home for all intermediates. Likely bottlenecks are L2/state traffic for direct-state scalar code, register pressure and synchronization for fully fused shared-exchange code, and redundant compute for token-owned fallback mappings.
open_questions: Does the evaluator expect PyTorch LayerNorm default eps=1e-5 with fp32 mean/variance and half output rounding at each module boundary, or is keeping fused intermediates in fp32 acceptable within rtol=0.01/atol=0.01?
Is HLSL float16_t arithmetic and typed Buffer<float16_t>/RWBuffer<float16_t> fully supported and performant in the runner for cs_6_8 on this path?
Which GELU form matches the reference closely enough: exact erf-based nn.GELU default or a tanh/polynomial approximation?
What is the actual baseline latency and scoring function, especially whether GPU timestamp excludes CPU staging and descriptor setup as stated?
Will direct SRV state reads be served efficiently from the 64 MB L2/constant path, or is explicit per-group read-only staging of qkv/proj/fc weights necessary despite the 32 KiB groupshared limit?
What threadgroup sizes and wave mappings does the HLSL compiler generate efficiently for small reductions over C=32, N=16, and hidden=128?
Are minor differences from Tensor Core matmul accumulation order in PyTorch tolerated for attention scores and linear layers under the 0.01 absolute/relative tolerance?
